title: BPR: Bayesian Personalized Ranking from Implicit Feedback (Variant 0)
abstract: We present a generic optimization criterion BPR-Opt for personalized ranking that is the maximum posterior estimator derived from a Bayesian analysis of the problem. We also provide a generic learning algorithm for optimizing models with respect to BPR-Opt.
problem: Personalized ranking from implicit feedback.
methodology: Maximum posterior estimator (BPR-Opt) and learn algorithm based on stochastic gradient descent.
findings: BPR outperforms standard matrix factorization techniques for item recommendation.
limitations: Assumes pairwise independence which may not hold in all scenarios.
future_work: Extend to context-aware recommendations.

title: Neural Collaborative Filtering (Variant 0)
abstract: We develop a neural network architecture to model latent features of users and items and devise a general framework NCF for collaborative filtering based on neural networks.
problem: Modeling non-linear interactions between users and items.
methodology: Combine GMF and MLP to learn user-item interactions.
findings: NCF significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods like BPR and eALS.
limitations: Computationally more expensive than shallow models.
future_work: Incorporate auxiliary information like reviews and context.

title: Deep Knowledge Tracing (Variant 0)
abstract: We apply Recurrent Neural Networks to the task of knowledge tracing. Our model, Deep Knowledge Tracing (DKT), handles the sequential nature of student interactions with educational software.
problem: Accurately modeling student knowledge over time.
methodology: Use LSTM to predict the probability of a student answering the next question correctly.
findings: DKT improves AUC significantly compared to Bayesian Knowledge Tracing.
limitations: Model lacks interpretability compared to traditional methods.
future_work: Explore attention mechanisms and incorporate skill hierarchies.

title: SASRec: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation (Variant 0)
abstract: We propose a sequential model based on self-attention mechanisms, which allows for capturing long-term semantics and predicting based on relatively few actions.
problem: Capturing both long-term semantics and short-term intents in sequences.
methodology: Use Transformer's self-attention to weight previous items in a sequence.
findings: SASRec outperforms CNN/RNN based models and is highly parallelizable.
limitations: Does not explicitly model time intervals between actions.
future_work: Incorporate context and timestamps into the attention mechanism.

title: A Contextual-Bandit Approach to Personalized News Article Recommendation (Variant 0)
abstract: We model personalized recommendation of news articles as a contextual bandit problem, and propose an algorithm, LinUCB, that selects articles based on user and article features.
problem: Cold-start recommendation and exploration-exploitation tradeoff.
methodology: Linear upper confidence bound algorithm with disjoint and hybrid models.
findings: LinUCB significantly increases click-through rates compared to random or epsilon-greedy.
limitations: Assumes linear relationship between features and expected reward.
future_work: Extend to non-linear payoff functions and dependent arms.

abstract: We apply Recurrent Neural Networks to the task of knowledge tracing. Our model, Deep Knowledge Tracing (DKT), handles the sequential nature of student interactions with educational software.
problem: Accurately modeling student knowledge over time.
methodology: Use LSTM to predict the probability of a student answering the next question correctly.
findings: DKT improves AUC significantly compared to Bayesian Knowledge Tracing.
limitations: Model lacks interpretability compared to traditional methods.
future_work: Explore attention mechanisms and incorporate skill hierarchies.

title: SASRec: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation (Variant 11)
abstract: We propose a sequential model based on self-attention mechanisms, which allows for capturing long-term semantics and predicting based on relatively few actions.
problem: Capturing both long-term semantics and short-term intents in sequences.
methodology: Use Transformer's self-attention to weight previous items in a sequence.
findings: SASRec outperforms CNN/RNN based models and is highly parallelizable.
limitations: Does not explicitly model time intervals between actions.
future_work: Incorporate context and timestamps into the attention mechanism.

title: A Contextual-Bandit Approach to Personalized News Article Recommendation (Variant 11)
abstract: We model personalized recommendation of news articles as a contextual bandit problem, and propose an algorithm, LinUCB, that selects articles based on user and article features.
problem: Cold-start recommendation and exploration-exploitation tradeoff.
methodology: Linear upper confidence bound algorithm with disjoint and hybrid models.
findings: LinUCB significantly increases click-through rates compared to random or epsilon-greedy.
limitations: Assumes linear relationship between features and expected reward.
future_work: Extend to non-linear payoff functions and dependent arms.
